collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A traveler comes home singing the farewell song with new verses: keep the new verses, or sing it as it was.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Twenty years ago, (subject) taught the village's farewell song to a young traveler leaving Isola. Today, (friend) has come home from the far islands, singing that same song, with seven new verses about places nobody here has ever seen. (subject) is not sure whether to be honored or upset. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village learns all the new verses: about ice that floats, birds that cannot fly, and a fish as long as a canoe. The song is now very long. (subject) adds a verse of (subject.his/her) own, about the song coming home.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village sings it as it always was. (friend) sings the new verses quietly, afterwards, for anyone who wants to hear them. The children want to hear them every night. Before long, everyone knows them anyway.
